Multi-ancestry placental xQTL analysis

Internal QC + R21 progress report

Bhattacharya Lab (analysis: S. Bresnahan; report generated with Biomni/Phylo)

2026-09-26

1 Executive summary

This report summarizes the multi-ancestry placental xQTL analysis: cohort-only genotype PCA on LD-pruned variants within each ancestry stratum, a conventional covariate set (first 5 genotype PCs + HCP factors + sex, gestational age, and cell-type fractions; maternal cell fraction excluded before correlation pruning at |r| > 0.9; HCP count optimized per ancestry via module 25a; no covariate cap), a MAF ≥ 0.01 filter with a ≥ 5 minor-allele-count floor at the genotype intersection, Storey q-values (computed with the R qvalue package), and per-phenotype rank-based inverse-normal transformation of all modalities (isoforms mapped as within-gene relative-abundance ratios). Mapping covers 32 ancestry × modality × layer cells (EAS n ≈ 272, EUR n ≈ 137).

Headline result: 8074 associations reach FDR ≤ 5% across the 32 ancestry × modality × layer cells. The primary eGene catalog (combined cross-modality layer) contains 1239 EAS and 1389 EUR eGenes at FDR ≤ 5%; per-modality grouped eGenes are the breakdown, and ungrouped phenotype-level hits are reported descriptively (Results). Strongest association per ancestry: EAS: ENSG00000290199 (expression, grouped layer, q = 2.4e-26); EUR: ERAP1 (alt_polyA, ungrouped layer, q = 4.4e-32). Outside the FDR-significant set, the best remaining q-value anywhere is 0.067. Storey calibration estimates a signal fraction (π1) of 0–33% across cells; at these fractions Storey q-values are numerically close to Benjamini–Hochberg (Diagnostics).

For the cells without FDR discoveries, three lines of evidence indicate the residual null is a power limitation, not a pipeline failure:

  1. Calibration is healthy — permutation-calibrated p-values track the null through the bulk in every layer (QQ plots, Diagnostics), and a low π1 is the expected outcome when true effects are mostly below the detection floor.
  2. Detectable effect sizes remain large at our n — minimum detectable effect (80% power) is r² ≈ 0.10 at n ≈ 272 (EAS) and r² ≈ 0.19 at n ≈ 137 (EUR), versus ≈ 0.06 at PANTRY/Geuvadis n = 445. Typical cis-xQTLs explain 5–15% of phenotype variance — mostly below our floor. The FDR-significant hits carry estimated r² of 0.00–0.74 — exactly the class of outsize effect the floor permits.
  3. Sub-threshold tails are not shared between ancestries — cross-ancestry rank concordance of gene-level signal is ≈ 0, as expected if near-misses are noise rather than shared weak signal.

Carrier-count caveat. A fraction of tested pairs retain < 5 minor-allele carriers in the mapping sample sets (EAS: 0 tests; EUR: 33445 tests; audit table below) — the MAC ≥ 5 floor was applied before outlier exclusion. Flagged tests should be discounted; no FDR-significant result should be carrier-limited.

2 Data and methods

2.1 Pipeline recap

  • Phenotypes: 8 RNA modalities (gene expression, isoform usage, splice junction usage, intron retention, alternative TSS, alternative polyA, RNA editing, RNA stability), harmonized to genotyped samples (array_id), with NIGMS technical replicates averaged per individual. The isoform modality is within-gene relative-abundance ratios (transcript TPM / gene-total TPM; PANTRY convention — QU-corrected Salmon counts, mean count ≥ 10 and mean ratio in [0.05, 0.95]), not isoform expression. Per ancestry stratum: feature filtering (isoforms: usage > 0.1 in > 25% of samples, devBrain §3.3 cadence; ratio modalities: detected in ≥ 40%, devBrain §3.4), batch-median NA imputation, quantile normalization across samples + rank-based inverse-normal transformation per phenotype, then ComBat (batch = cohort) last — the devBrain “ComBat on the normalized data” convention. No log2 pre-transform is applied: rank-based INT is invariant to any monotone transform, so log2/VST would be exact no-ops on the mapped scale.
  • Genotypes: ancestry-stratified plink2 pgen; variants filtered to MAF ≥ 0.01 with MAC ≥ 5 (≥ 5 minor alleles) at the genotype intersection — the count floor excludes low-carrier tests, which can produce spurious associations, while MAF 0.01 keeps the variant pool as large as defensible. tensorQTL’s own MAF ≥ 0.01 filter applies on top at mapping time.
  • Genotype PCA: cohort-only PCA per ancestry on LD-pruned variants (plink2 --indep-pairwise 200 50 0.2, then --pca 20 exact) — the GTEx convention.
  • Covariates: per ancestry, first-5 genotype PCs + HCP factors 1–k* (k* selected by module 25a, chr1 eGene maximization) + sex + gestational age + cell-type fractions (Syncytiotrophoblast as reference). The maternal cell-fraction covariate (ct_Maternal) is excluded BEFORE pruning by analysis decision (coded --exclude-covariates, replacing the round-3 hand-edit); the remaining pool is correlation-pruned (iterative max-|r| > 0.9 removal, protecting sex/GA > PCs > cell types > HCPs — correlated HCPs are dropped, so effective k can fall below nominal k*) with no covariate cap (details and QC below).
  • Mapping (tensorQTL, cis window ±1 Mb): (i) per-modality grouped — all phenotypes of a gene within a modality tested as one group (permutation-calibrated gene-level p-value; the row label is the driver phenotype); (ii) combined — all phenotypes of a gene across all modalities as one cross-modality group (PANTRY’s headline design); (iii) ungrouped — per-phenotype lead variants for transcript-level resolution; (iv) stepwise (cis.map_independent) for conditionally independent signals, entered at FDR ≤ 5%.
  • Multiple testing: Storey q-values on the permutation-calibrated p-value (pval_beta), computed with the R qvalue package (default lambda) — the GTEx convention, and statistically identical to tensorQTL’s own calculate_qvalues. (On this cluster the rpy2/conda-R route to qvalue hits an unresolvable libstdc++/GLIBCXX conflict, so q-values are computed through a file-based bridge to the singularity R container used elsewhere in the pipeline.)

Outlier exclusion on the cohort-only PCs (6-SD rule on PC1–PC5) removed 1 EAS and 5 EUR samples. Pruning dropped 2 covariates in EAS (1 excluded, 1 reference_cell_type) and 2 in EUR (1 excluded, 1 reference_cell_type); both ancestries retained all of PC1–PC5: TRUE, TRUE. Correlated-HCP drops (if any) reduce effective k below the nominal 25a optimum — see the HCP-optimization section.

Scree plots (cohort-only PCA, LD-pruned variants): PC1 carries ≈ 13–14% of pruned-variant variance in both strata, with a smooth, shallow decay thereafter (PC2 ≈ 6–9%) and no sharp elbow — the expected spectrum within ancestry-stratified subsets, and the basis for the first-5-PCs rule.

Covariate correlation matrices before/after pruning: no |r| > 0.9 pairs remain in the final sets.

2.3 HCP count optimization (module 25a)

Module 25a re-estimates HCPs at each candidate k on the pruned fixed covariate set (no cap), maps the chr1 expression layer per k, and selects k* by eGene yield: EAS k* = 25 (115 eGenes), EUR k* = 15 (135 eGenes). The k* solution is installed as the canonical harmonized HCP file for module 25.

3.3 Phenotypes per gene group (PANTRY Fig 2b adapted)

Stepwise regression (cis.map_independent) ran on 6349 FDR-qualifying groups; 423 group(s) carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (rank ≥ 2). The design-level view below shows how many phenotypes each gene contributes to its group (the multiple-testing unit).

Combined groups integrate a median of ~4–5 phenotypes per gene (max > 100) — the cross-modality burden-sharing the PANTRY design exploits. (Stability shows a flat box at 1 by design: one phenotype per gene.)

Densities are computed over the top 200 genes per layer (FDR-significant plus sub-threshold); read as a positional summary of the strongest signals.

4 Calibration and diagnostics

4.1 Permutation-calibrated p-value QQ plots

Calibrated p-values track the null through the bulk with at most a modest short tail — the signature of few-or-no detectable associations, without systematic inflation (which would bend the whole curve up) or deflation.

At n ≈ 137 (EUR), only xQTLs explaining ≳ 19% of phenotype variance are detectable at genome-wide thresholds; the larger EAS stratum (n ≈ 272) brings the floor to ≈ 10% — versus ≈ 6% at PANTRY’s n = 445. For reference, PANTRY (n = 445) reported 6,798 eGenes and a 66% discovery gain from non-expression modalities; GTEx tissues at n ≈ 150 typically report hundreds to ~2,000 eGenes. Our yield this round (8074 FDR ≤ 5% associations; 2628 combined-layer eGenes) sits within that range.

The MAC ≥ 5 floor is applied at the genotype intersection in module 23 (before outlier exclusion). A fraction of tests retain < 5 carriers in the mapping sample sets (audit table) because the floor predates outlier exclusion and modality-specific sample attrition. No FDR-significant result should be carrier-limited; hit lists should be post-filtered to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source.

5.4 Stepwise regression: independent signals

Of the 6349 FDR-qualifying groups entering the stepwise scan, 423 carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (rank ≥ 2); the remainder yielded their primary lead variant alone.

8 Transcript-level driver resolution

The combined layer labels each gene-group by its driver phenotype (the phenotype with the best nominal association in the group), and the ungrouped layer provides per-phenotype lead variants. Applied to the FDR-significant catalog, this resolves which modality and transcript carries each eGene signal.

9 Biological interpretation

The discovery landscape this round: 8074 FDR ≤ 5% associations — 1239 EAS and 1389 EUR eGenes in the primary combined-layer catalog (n ≈ 272/137, MAF ≥ 0.01 + MAC ≥ 5, genome-wide permutation calibration). Strongest per ancestry: EAS: ENSG00000290199 (expression, grouped layer, q = 2.4e-26, r² ≈ 0.42); EUR: ERAP1 (alt_polyA, ungrouped layer, q = 4.4e-32, r² ≈ 0.68). Hit effect sizes (r² 0.00–0.74) sit in the class the power floor permits. All hits should be treated as candidates: visual QC of phenotype levels by genotype and replication in larger placental cohorts come before functional claims.

Three characterization observations:

  1. Modality composition. expression leads the EAS grouped-eGene breakdown (1127 of 1620); expression leads the EUR grouped-eGene breakdown (1298 of 1979) PANTRY’s central finding was that non-expression modalities carry the largest share of regulatory signal; the driver-modality composition of the catalog (above) tests whether that ordering holds in placenta.
  2. Ancestry sharing. 495 of 1237 EAS and 1388 EUR combined-layer eGenes are shared (Fisher OR 7.71, p = 1.1e-177 vs the tested-in-both universe). Shared eGenes are the cross-ancestry replication signal; specific sets are candidates for ancestry-biased regulation.
  3. Functional enrichment. Top g:Profiler term per set: EAS combined eGenes — extracellular region (GO:CC, g:SCS p = 6.4e-05); EUR combined eGenes — extracellular region (GO:CC, g:SCS p = 0.00061); shared eGenes — Post-translational modification: synthesis of GPI-anchored proteins (REAC, g:SCS p = 0.0016). Full tables in tables/enrichment_*.tsv.

Sub-threshold top-ranked genes (tables above) remain prioritization hints only — and the flagged low-carrier rows should be discounted outright.

10 Limitations and next steps

  1. Power. n ≈ 272/137 with a ~12k-gene testing burden detects only r² ≳ 0.10 (EAS) / 0.19 (EUR) effects. Doubling n would roughly halve the detectable r²; matching PANTRY’s n = 445 would bring the floor to ≈ 0.06. Adding the remaining cohorts and the AFR/AMR/SAS strata is the highest-value next step.
  2. Carrier-count propagation. The MAC ≥ 5 floor predates outlier exclusion, so low-carrier tests persist in some mapping outputs (audit table above). No reported result depends on them; hit lists should post-filter to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source.
  3. Ancestry asymmetry. EUR tests more phenotypes than EAS in every modality (ancestry-specific filtering), so cross-ancestry comparisons are restricted to genes tested in both.
  4. No pooled cross-ancestry inference was performed. If combined discovery is wanted later, Fisher/Stouffer or an inverse-variance slope meta-analysis are the clean options.
  5. Stepwise secondary signals: 423 groups carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (table above).
  6. Fine-mapping and colocalization are out of scope this round. The natural follow-ups on the FDR-significant catalog are SuSiE fine-mapping per eGene locus, GWAS colocalization (coloc/eCAVIAR) against placental and pregnancy-outcome GWAS, and locus-zoom visual QC of each hit (nominal-scan extraction + LD from the ancestry-matched genotype panel).
  7. Replication path: the FDR-significant hits are the priorities for lookup in larger placental resources or a future meta-analysis; visual QC of phenotype levels by genotype is the immediate sanity check for each.

11 Reproducibility

  • Results: tensorQTL cis mapping (grouped / ungrouped / combined / stepwise), MAF ≥ 0.01 + MAC ≥ 5 at the genotype intersection, ±1 Mb window, Storey q-values on pval_beta via the R qvalue package (singularity-R bridge). Covariates: as described (first-5 PCs + HCP_1–k* + sex/GA/cell types; maternal fraction excluded before correlation pruning; no cap). Genotype PCs: cohort-only plink2 PCA on LD-pruned variants.
  • Pipeline scripts: this repository (05_qtl_mapping/, scripts 19–30 + compute_qvalues.R; genotype pooling in 01_genotype_imputation/).
  • Report code: report_placenta_xqtl.Rmd + xqtl_report_functions.R; figures in figures/, tables in tables/.
  • Gene symbols: gene_map.tsv regenerated in full from the normalized GTF (config normalized_gtf) by make_report_archive.sh at archive time — covers every tested gene, version-stripped IDs.
